method.latency: Nanoseconds per complete call, including returned-value destruction. Lower is better.
method.throughput: Decimal MB/s (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes). Loads uses original input bytes; dumps uses output bytes. Higher is better.
method.preparation: Standard-library json.loads creates identical Python values. Downloads, file reads, hashing, preparation, and correctness checks are outside timing.
method.correctness: For requested operations, compare complete values and exact types, float bits, dictionary order, and encoded bytes across all builds before timing. Recheck each worker before measuring.
method.geomean: For each unique case, divide a library's median process latency by the reference's median process latency. Take the geometric mean of those ratios with equal case weights. Lower is better; 1 means equal latency.
method.duplicates: Loads deduplicates identical document SHA-256s. Dumps also deduplicates identical encoded outputs after exact-value checks. duplicate_cases lists omitted cases.
method.gc: Cyclic GC is collected and disabled around warmup/calibration/timing; reference-counted result destruction remains timed.
method.cache: Repeated calls use the same prepared input. These are warm repeated-call measurements, not cold-cache or startup measurements.

publication_selection.schedule_note: This is a selection from a four-build session, not a new two-build run. Each run retains the selected libraries' positions in the original worker order.
publication_selection.summary_note: Summaries were recomputed from unchanged selected samples and checked against the original values.
